Describe a dataset safely

profile_data.Rd

profile_data() records what is needed to make a convincing copy and nothing that identifies a person. It describes one table or a set of linked tables and applies the protection rules before anything is stored, so the result can be saved with saveRDS() and taken out of the secure environment. mimic() builds the synthetic copy from it.

Usage

profile_data(tables, keys = NULL, config = NULL, main = NULL)

Arguments

tables

A data frame, or a named list of linked data frames.

keys

Key linking the tables: one column name used in every table, or a named character vector mapping table names to key columns. Persons are counted on this key.

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults.

main

Name of the table with one row per person. By default the first table whose key is unique.

Value

An object of class mimic_profile with elements tables (variable descriptions per table), keys, n_persons (rounded), config and risk (a risk report, see Details).

Details

The risk report ($risk) lists every variable that protection changed and how, checks combinations of quasi-identifiers with check_k_anonymity() (totals only), checks the keys with check_keys(), and says whether the population is too small for synthesis above level 2 (min_persons). Variables that were classified as identifiers or free text automatically are reported with a warning, so a wrong guess is noticed.

What is stored

For every variable: name, type, share missing, and depending on type

  • categorical (character, factor): allowed values and rounded frequencies. Categories with fewer than min_count persons are merged into other_label; if the merged group itself is too small, the next smallest category is merged too. Factor levels that no one holds are dropped: they are labels of fewer than min_count persons as well, and may come from a list outside the data.

  • geographical (geo_vars): as categorical, flagged so that small units (settlements) are reported.

  • numeric: bottom and top coded bounds, a coarse histogram whose bins each hold at least min_count persons, and rounded mean, median and standard deviation computed after top and bottom coding. Integer variables with few values keep their values as bins.

  • dates: as numeric, with bounds coarsened to date_unit and bins by year.

  • logical: rounded frequencies; a value held by fewer than min_count persons is suppressed.

  • identifiers (keys, id_vars, and columns that look like ids): the format only, such as "A9999999". Letters or punctuation shared by every value are kept only when at least min_persons values share them; digits never are.

  • free text (text_vars, and long character columns that are mostly unique): only the approximate length.

  • names and addresses: a categorical variable with at least 20 categories, more than half of them held by fewer than min_count persons, is stored as an identifier. Its few common values are households or blocks of flats, which is not a category to publish. To keep a code like this as categories, coarsen it first (the first characters of a code, a district instead of an address). This applies to geo_vars too: a geographical unit where most units hold fewer than min_count persons is an address, not a place.

For linked tables it also stores the distribution of rows per person (top coded), the share of persons with no rows, and the share of rows that refer to unknown persons.

For level 3 of mimic() each table also gets a correlation matrix of the normal scores of its variables on the protected scale, with the rows per person in linked tables added for the main table. It is rounded to one decimal and only stored with at least min_persons persons. Correlation coefficients belong to the "safe" output classes in the Eurostat guidelines for output checking.

All counting is done in persons, not rows: a category held by one person with twenty contacts is still a category of one person.

Why bounds are not the 1 % quantile

With 40 rows, the 1 % quantile is one person's value. profile_data() therefore places each bound where at least max(tail_coding * persons, min_count) persons lie at or beyond it.

What is never stored

Rows, identifier values, free text, exact minima and maxima, and labels of categories held by fewer than min_count persons. Counts below min_count are suppressed and other counts rounded to round_base.

Examples

cfg <- mimic_config(
  quasi_ids = c("birth_date", "sex", "settlement"),
  geo_vars = "settlement",
  text_vars = "note"
)
m <- profile_data(
  list(persons = fake_persons, contacts = fake_contacts,
       admissions = fake_admissions),
  keys = "person_id",
  config = cfg
)
m
#> <mimic_profile> 3 tables, about 2,000 persons
